title: 2005 HMMT February Geometry Problem 4
statement: Let \(X Y Z\) be a triangle with \(\angle X=60^{\circ}\) and \(\angle Y=45^{\circ}\). A circle with center \(P\) passes through points \(A\) and \(B\) on side \(X Y, C\) and \(D\) on side \(Y Z\), and \(E\) and \(F\) on side \(Z X\). Suppose \(A B=C D=E F\). Find \(\angle X P Y\) in degrees.

solutions.text:
\(255 / 2\)

Since \(P A B, P C D\), and \(P E F\) are all isosceles triangles with equal legs and equal bases, they are congruent. It follows that the heights of each are the same, so that \(P\) is equidistant from the sides of \(X Y Z\). Therefore, \(P\) is the incenter and therefore lies on the angle bisectors of \(X Y Z\). Thus \(\angle Y X P=\frac{1}{2} \angle Y X Z=30^{\circ}\) and \(\angle P Y X=\frac{1}{2} \angle Z Y X=\) \(\frac{45^{\circ}}{2}\). Therefore \(\angle X P Y=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}-\frac{45^{\circ}}{2}=\frac{255^{\circ}}{2}\).
